decision: Accept eight-worker joined-input variant; reject sixteen-worker variant whose whole-model gain was negligible.
design: Unpack each 4160-byte INT8 tile once to exact BF16 integer values; reuse for two tokens. Per-row FP16-expanded scales apply only after all eight K tiles. This is W8A16 with BF16 MAC, not native INT8 MAC.
Join strided two-token projection input and separate residual BOs on a MemTile. Each compute worker receives joined activation and weight streams, satisfying its two input DMA channel limit.
Fuse residual addition into each projection worker. Process token 1 first during in-place output expansion so token 0 residual stores cannot overwrite token 1 projection.
Use existing paired activation/output allocations. Host payload, resident BO bytes and root BO count unchanged.
capacity_evidence: Direct four-input-stream fused worker failed placement: core has only two input DMA channels. MemTile staging resolves this without host copies.

stage.oracle: FP64 dot on BF16-rounded inputs, then row scale; tolerance 2e-5 + 2e-5*abs(reference).
stage.bitwise: Each token projection and residual equals the original INT8 output kernel. All allocation guards passed.

protocol.order: A/B/B/A per design, serial NPU dispatch

bf16_compiler_compatibility: Final shared compiler BF16 stages pass oracle/bitwise/guards for all three strides. Resident-stride instruction binaries and extracted PDIs are byte-identical to production; xclbin container bytes differ.
limitations: Measured decode mean increases about 0.14%; decode still uses the original kernels and 123 submissions. Do not present this as a decode speedup.
Local compute utilization, internal DDR traffic and device bandwidth counters were not measured.
FP32 recurrence remains sequential across tokens; whole-model hardware limits remain unproven.
